title: Plug the leak
description:
`spawnWave(count, blocked)` creates `count` monsters and returns the ones that could be placed. A monster is placed unless its index appears in `blocked`. Monsters that cannot be placed are thrown away.

It gives the right answers, but every monster that cannot be placed is leaked. The tests check for leaks. Fix it so that nothing leaks, and keep it returning a `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Monster>>`.
hints: The leak happens on the `continue`: `m` is a raw pointer, and nobody deletes what it points to.
If the monster is owned by a `std::unique_ptr` from the very start, leaving the loop body by any route frees it.
rules: Do not use new: create each monster with std::make_unique so it is owned from the moment it exists.
lessonTitle: Memory Bugs: Overruns, Dangling Pointers and Leaks

rules.message: Do not use new: create each monster with std::make_unique so it is owned from the moment it exists.
